name: Cherokee syllabary and its community use
description: A syllabic writing system developed by Sequoyah for the Cherokee language and adopted for Cherokee community writing and print.

date.label: 1821–1825, date disputed
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: Smithsonian accounts date Cherokee Nation adoption of Sequoyah’s syllabary to 1821 and 1825 respectively.
events.caveats: The interval reflects conflicting accounts rather than a dated sequence of continuous adoption; the underlying council record needs inspection.

contributions.resource: Adopted the Cherokee writing system according to the cited accounts.
Created the syllabary adopted by Cherokee leaders.

evidence.supports: Credits Sequoyah with creating and teaching the syllabary.
The festival publication states adoption in 1821.

date.label: 21 February 1828
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: The Cherokee Phoenix began publication at New Echota in Cherokee and English.
events.population: Readers of the Cherokee Nation’s bilingual newspaper

evidence.supports: The museum dates and locates the first bilingual issue.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest cited dated event for this scoped record; a surviving witness or publication is not itself the invention date.

places.note: New Echota in present-day Georgia; this country label is a modern geographic reference, not an attribution of Cherokee governance to the United States.

caveats: The Cherokee system is a distinct community achievement; its creation was informed by contact with existing writing, so independent invention of writing in general is not asserted.

research.note: Second reader checked Smithsonian 1825 educational guide and 1828 newspaper account. The 1821 account remains to be independently opened; apparent disagreement and possible different adoption milestones remain unresolved.

impact.note: The Cherokee Nation adopted a system used in law and newspapers.

tier_reason: Provisional judgment of sourced consequences, following docs/importance.md; independent review required.
